name: Moonlit Sanctuary Wildlife Conservation Park
pickupPoints: Moonlit Sanctuary, 550 Tyabb-Tooradin Road, Pearcedale VIC 3912
intro: Moonlit Sanctuary is a conservation wildlife park at Pearcedale, specialising in threatened Australian native species including eastern quolls, bettongs, brush-tailed phascogales, koalas, and little penguins. The park operates a captive breeding programme for several species listed under the EPBC Act. Its flagship offering is the guided Twilight Tour, a nocturnal walk held after dark when the resident animals are most active and accessible.
whatGoodAt: Delivering close-contact encounters with Australian native animals, particularly nocturnal species that most visitors never see in the wild. The guided format ensures guests understand the conservation context behind what they are seeing. Strong for families with children aged 4 and above, school groups, and international visitors experiencing species like quolls and phascogales for the first time.
notSuitedFor: Guests expecting a large zoo-scale experience with many species and free-roaming exploration. Self-directed visitors who prefer to explore without a guide. Groups wanting a wildlife show format without the conservation emphasis.
